metadata.goal: Analyze the pickup-work patterns of multiple couriers from their trajectories and accepted pickup tasks.
metadata.category: pickup time-window reliability, task timing, and spatial concentration
metadata.header: Multi-Courier Pickup Time Windows and Reliability
metadata.dataset_description: This case uses the original LaDe-P field semantics: accept_time, time_window_start, time_window_end, pickup_time, acceptance/pickup GPS positions, region_id, and AOI attributes. Five couriers each have a continuous GPS trajectory and twelve accepted pickup tasks. All reliability and duration outcomes must be computed from the primitive event times.

insight_list.question: How do acceptance timing, actual pickup duration, and completion within the planned service window vary together across the pickup tasks?

insight_list.insight: Short pickup durations do not necessarily correspond to higher reliability, as some rapidly completed tasks still violate their promised time windows.

insights: Later-accepted pickup tasks are not only completed faster but are also more likely to fall within their promised service windows.
Short pickup durations do not necessarily correspond to higher reliability, as some rapidly completed tasks still violate their promised time windows.
Time-window violations are driven predominantly by pickups completed before the allowed window rather than by delayed completion.
Early pickups are spatially concentrated in a small set of recurring regions.
summary: Later-accepted pickup tasks in this multi-courier sample are generally shorter and more likely to be completed within their planned windows. However, rapid completion is not always reliable: most violations are early pickups, and all early pickups concentrate in three recurring service regions.
